hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Easier one: $x^2 + 5x + 6$ needs two numbers multiplying to $6$ and adding to $5$; that is $2$ and $3$. Yours needs a NEGATIVE product.
The numbers must multiply to $-6$ and add to $-1$. Test pairs with opposite signs: $-6$ and $1$ add to $-5$, so try $-3$ and $2$.
$-3 \times 2 = -6$ and $-3 + 2 = -1$, so the factored form is $(x - 3)(x + 2)$.

explanation: To factor $x^2 - x - 6$, find two numbers whose product is $-6$ and whose sum is $-1$.
A negative product means one number is positive and the other is negative.
The pair $-3$ and $2$ works, because $-3 \times 2 = -6$ and $-3 + 2 = -1$.
Those numbers go into the brackets, so $x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sign detective
steps: Product negative → the two numbers have DIFFERENT signs.
Sum negative → the bigger-sized number wears the minus.
Pairs for 6: (1, 6) and (2, 3). Only −3 and +2 sum to −1.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check by expanding
steps: Combine: x² − x − 6. It matches the original, so the factoring is right.
